samples.text: Floating-point addition is not associative because rounding errors introduced during each arithmetic operation can vary depending on the order of computation. For example, (a + b) + c may yield a different result than a + (b + c) due to intermediate rounding. This occurs because floating-point numbers have limited precision, so the order in which additions are performed affects which bits are lost during rounding.

Floating-point addition is not associative because the finite precision of floating-point representations introduces rounding errors that depend on the order of operations. When adding three numbers, the intermediate result of the first two may be rounded differently depending on which pair is added first, leading to different final results. For example, (a + b) + c may yield a different value than a + (b + c) due to these accumulated rounding discrepancies.
